dedupe_keys.name: associated british ports fourth round climate change adaptation report humber immingham hull and southampton

description: Associated British Ports (ABP) publishes this fourth round climate change adaptation report under the UK Climate Change Act 2008, which directs it to report voluntarily on its role as harbour authority for the Humber, Immingham, Hull and Southampton. Coverage: the Humber ports handle trade the page values at about £86 billion, and Southampton, the UK's largest export port, number one vehicle handling port and leading turnaround cruise port, handles about £40 billion of trade and supports 45,600 jobs. Findings: ABP names sea level rise as the biggest climate risk to its harbour authority operations, notes continued uncertainty about storm frequency and intensity, and says its operations cannot move away from the coast, so flood risk will rise; it describes operational procedures, flood resilience and renewable energy investment under its 'Ready for Tomorrow' strategy, and calls for Government support through planning and flood and coastal erosion risk management. Format and access: a summary web page linking the full report. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: the full report was not read here, and trade figures are ABP's own. It frames sea level rise exposure and adaptation choices for climate adaptation and hazard exposure studies of UK estuary ports. It relates to the PLA and Felixstowe adaptation reports in the catalogue.
